answer: Expose the three primitives zmx already gives, document the trust boundary, and build no coordination layer: labels as the board (`state=` for attention, freeform tokens for anything else), `zmx print` for out-of-band text a human will see, and name prefixes + ZMX_DIR for grouping and isolation. The trust boundary is one user, or a group sharing a socket dir via ZMX_DIR_MODE — in which case any member can attach, label and kill, and the labels are a lying channel. That is stated as a limit, not fixed.
body: How much of the shared world to expose, and where the 'wildly insecure and Fun' line sits.
title: How much of the shared world do we expose?
